newsitem.title: HUNGARY: INTERVIEW - Hungary's Matav telecoms mulls IPO.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Hungary's Matav telecoms mulls IPO.

text.p: Hungarian telecommunications company Matav Rt is still talking to different investment banks about the possibility of an initial public offering (IPO), an official said on Monday.
Matav's chief financial officer Ray Stewart told Reuters in an interview about the company's capital investment plans and commented on market speculation of an equity offering in 1997.
Stewart, an American, declined to confirm a Financial Times report that Matav was set to name Merrill Lynch to lead an international equity offering.
"We are still talking to different banks about a possible role, in a possible Matav IPO, but no decision has been made yet," he said.
Stewart said he hoped that the choice of a financial adviser would be made by end January.

Geza Laszlo chief economist of Matav's financial arm, Investel, said last November that CS First Boston, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley are shortlisted to be the financial adviser.
Stewart said it was premature to discuss the size of a public offering since there was as yet no decision on whether there would be an IPO.

"Once that decision has been made, it has to be decided whether it is MagyarCom that would sell shares, is it the government or is it the company issuing new equity?" he said. "All of these impact the size.".
Deutsche Telekom AG and Ameritech Corp together bought 30 percent of Matav in 1993 for $850 million and purchased another 37 percent of the company in late 1995 for $852 million.

The Hungarian government holds a 25 percent stake with the remainder held by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the International Finance Corporation, local governments and individual investors.
An analyst said the market is looking forward to a Matav offering which could be all the more attractive if the state also decides to sell some of its stake.
"It could be a share package of some $1 billion, which would be the biggest Hungarian offering so far," said Rudi Voros, London-based analyst of ICE Securities.
He added that Matav has had good results when compared to other telecommunications companies in central Europe.

"The only other company in the region it could be compared with is the Czech Republic's SPT Telecom," Voros said. "Although SPT also invests very large amounts in its network, I think Matav is ahead of them."

Matav said in October it expected profits of more that 12 billion forints ($73.9 million) in 1996 on net sales of 190 billion forints compared with a net profit of 293 million forints on sales of 135.5 billion in 1995. The company made vast capital outlays in 1995 to upgrade its ageing system and to expand.
Based on net sales ranking, Matav was the third biggest Hungarian company in 1995, behind oil and gas company MOL Rt and electricity company MVM.
Stewart said they plan a capital investment programme of some $400 to $500 million this year, mainly on network improvement.
"We will build new lines, new digital exchanges and will also put in additional data line and data processing for businesses," Stewart said. ($ = 162.4 Hungarian Forints)
